samples.summary: New MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32 duplicates the existing MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32 in the same package, which already answers the same question ("how deep will a reader descend a peer-written nested-table chain?")
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111` already exports `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32`, documented at lines 100-110 and enforced at line 408 (`if (Array.isArray(cell.blocks) && depth < MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH)`) with the comment "Capped rather than trusted: a nested-table chain a peer wrote is unbounded, and the stack this walk would blow is the reader's whole read()". `docs/design/docs/docs.md:290-298` documents this cap as the repo's policy for nested-table recursion ("The group recursion is depth-capped at 32 ... `bandBlockNumerics` carries the same cap on its own nested-table recursion (`MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`)"). The diff adds a second, independently-named constant with the same value and the same rationale in a brand-new module, exported from both `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts`. The two are now coupled in fact but not in code: `bandBlockNumerics` stops banding numerics below depth 32 while `treeNodeToBlock`/`layoutCellBlocks` stop *reading/laying out* at their own 32, so changing either one alone yields blocks that a reader materialises but the bander never banded (re-opening the very `Infinity` row-height hazard `numeric-attrs.ts` closes) — two answers to one question. Reuse was trivially available: `numeric-attrs.ts` is already exported from the same barrels the diff edits.

samples.summary: A hard nesting cap that silently truncates table rows contradicts a stated Goal of the nested-tables design doc, and no design doc under docs/design/ was added or updated to record the new invariant
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:19` states as a Goal: "Recursive nesting with no hard depth limit (UI naturally limits via minimum cell width of 30 px)", and its Risks table (line 275) repeats "Minimum column width (30 px) naturally limits depth". The diff introduces exactly such a hard limit at both the CRDT read boundary and the layout, and past it a table is read/laid out with no rows at all — i.e. content below level 32 is not rendered. That is a model-level invariant change with a user-visible (if remote) consequence, and CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline expects it folded into the canonical subsystem doc (`docs-nested-tables.md`, or the peer-writable-numbers section of `docs/design/docs/docs.md:198-298` where the sibling `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` cap is already designed). Nothing in the diff touches `docs/design/`. Note also the divergence in policy: `docs.md:297` says at the cap the walk "stop[s] descending and leave[s] what is below as stored", whereas the new cap drops the rows from the materialised document.

samples.summary: Scope creep: a #1049 nested-table/merge selection fix is bundled with three unrelated hardening projects (nesting depth cap, five parent-chain cycle guards, peer cell-range index clamping)
samples.evidence: The issue-linked work (nested-aware `tableData` lookup in `normalizeRange`/`getSelectedText`/`getSelectedTableCells`, the shared `resolveCellGesture` for drag vs shift+click) is self-contained. The diff additionally lands: `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` in the CRDT reader, the frontend `YorkieDocStore` reader and `computeTableLayout`/`layoutCellBlocks`; cycle guards in `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `resolvePositionPixel`, `Doc.findBlockInCells`, `findOuterCellAddress`, `findOutermostTableId`; and `clampCellIndex`/`normalizeCellRange` bounding of peer-written `tableCellRange` indices plus loop bounds in `buildCellRangeRects`. None of these are needed to make the reported selection behaviour correct; each is a distinct hardening concern that would be separately reviewable (and separately design-documented, per the previous finding).

samples.summary: The nested-aware table lookup idiom is copy-pasted into four new call sites instead of being factored into one helper next to resolveNestedTableLayout
samples.evidence: `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === X)?.block.tableData ?? resolveNestedTableLayout(X, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` now appears at `selection.ts` ~190 (`normalizeRange`), ~835 and ~864 (`getSelectedText`, twice) and `text-editor.ts` ~4330 (`getSelectedTableCells`), each with its own explanatory comment. The repo already centralises this resolution in `resolveNestedTableLayout` (`view/table-layout.ts`, also used pre-existing at `text-editor.ts:4379`); one exported `resolveTableData(blockId, layout)` would keep the four sites from drifting the next time the flat/nested precedence changes. Cost stays inside the codebase, hence minor.

samples.summary: Six separate hand-written copies of the same guarded blockParentMap ancestor walk, when a guarded walk helper already exists in the package
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:74-92` already implements `topLevelBlockId(doc, blockId)` — the same climb with the same `seen` guard and the same documented rationale. The diff writes the guard again, independently, in `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts ~508), `resolvePositionPixel` (peer-cursor.ts ~122), `walkToTopLevelBlockId` (selection.ts, new), `findOutermostTableId` (text-editor.ts, new), `findOuterCellAddress` (text-editor.ts ~3894) and `Doc.findBlockInCells` (document.ts ~270). The variants already differ in stop condition and in what they return on a cycle (`undefined` vs. the last id vs. falling through to a full-document walk), so a future correction to one will not reach the others. No behavioural cost today.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence checks out verbatim. `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` exists at packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111, documented at 97-110 as the nested-table-cell recursion cap and enforced at line 408 with the quoted "Capped rather than trusted: a nested-table chain a peer wrote is unbounded" comment. The diff adds a second, independently-named constant with the identical value and a rationale naming the same hazard at packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26 (header lines 2-24 explicitly liken it to the numeric bands), enforced at crdt-tree.ts:225, view/table-layout.ts:145 and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:480, and exported from both src/index.ts:97 and src/node.ts:145. docs/design/docs/docs.md:290-298 documents the 32 cap as repo policy naming only MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH; no design doc mentions MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH. The coupling claim is also real: bandBlockNumerics bands slide/board bodies (slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:89,95,107,219) whose Blocks then reach layoutCellBlocks, so the band cap and the layout cap gate the same chain from two uncoordinated constants — change one and blocks get laid out that were never banded. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described (not not-present), nothing couples or guards the two values (not already-guarded), and duplication/reuse is explicitly this lens's lane with reuse trivially available (numeric-attrs.ts is DOM-free, same package, already on both barrels per node.ts:146-149), so the cross-package "copy" justification that excuses MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH itself does not apply here.
